position: before its word — almost always *small*, *rare* or *few*
modifies: adjectives of size and number: *small*, *rare*, *few*, *thin*

senses.gloss: So little that it almost does not exist.
examples: The chances of that happening are *vanishingly* small.
Cases like his are *vanishingly* rare.
The number of voters who changed their minds was *vanishingly* small.

position: mid — before a participle (*variously described as*)
modifies: past participles of describing, estimating and naming

senses.gloss: In different ways, by different people or at different times.
examples: He has been *variously* described as a genius and a fraud.
The crowd was *variously* estimated at 5,000 to 10,000 people.
The town's name is *variously* spelled on old maps.

position: before its word — before adjectives and comparatives (*vastly different*, *vastly better*); mid before a verb (*vastly improved*)
modifies: adjectives, comparatives and verbs of change

senses.gloss: Very much; to a very great degree.
examples: The two cities are *vastly* different.
Her new job is *vastly* better paid than the old one.
The software has *vastly* improved since last year.

position: mid or end — before verbs of denying and opposing (*vehemently denied*)
modifies: verbs of denying, opposing, arguing and objecting

senses.gloss: With very strong feeling, especially in disagreeing.
examples: He *vehemently* denied the accusations.
Local residents are *vehemently* opposed to the new highway.
She argued *vehemently* against the plan.

position: end
modifies: verbs

senses.gloss: In a way that shows a wish to get revenge.
examples: He smiled *vengefully* as his rival lost the election.
The fired employee acted *vengefully* and deleted the company's files.
She glared *vengefully* at the referee.

position: end
modifies: verbs of speaking, writing and looking

senses.gloss: With bitter hatred or spite.
examples: "Get out of my house," she said *venomously*.
He wrote *venomously* about his former business partners.
The two candidates attacked each other *venomously*.

position: end — or mid before a verb or participle (*verbally abused*)
modifies: verbs and past participles

senses.gloss: With words rather than actions or physical force.
examples: The referee was *verbally* abused by angry fans.
He *verbally* attacked the reporter during the press conference.
She never hit anyone, but she was *verbally* aggressive.

senses.gloss: In speech rather than in writing.
examples: We agreed *verbally*, but nothing was signed.
The warning was given *verbally* before the written notice arrived.

position: end
modifies: verbs of quoting, copying and repeating
form: from Latin; the same form is an adjective (*a verbatim record*)

senses.gloss: In exactly the same words.
examples: She repeated his words *verbatim*.
The student copied whole paragraphs *verbatim* from a website.
I'm quoting the email *verbatim* here.

position: end
modifies: verbs of writing, speaking and explaining

senses.gloss: Using more words than needed.
examples: He writes *verbosely*, and his reports are hard to follow.
The instructions were *verbosely* written and confusing.
She explained the rule *verbosely* when one sentence would have done.

position: end
modifies: verbs

senses.gloss: Straight up and down, at a right angle to the ground.
examples: Cut the pepper in half *vertically*.
Hold the bottle *vertically* while you pour.
The title runs *vertically* down the side of the page.

position: end — most often in *live vicariously through*
modifies: verbs like *live*, *enjoy*, *experience*, *travel*

senses.gloss: By watching or hearing about someone else's experiences instead of having them yourself.
examples: Some parents live *vicariously* through their kids.
I travel *vicariously* by following my friend's trip online.
We enjoyed the concert *vicariously* through her photos.

position: end — or mid before a participle (*viciously attacked*)
modifies: verbs and past participles

senses.gloss: In a cruel, violent or very hostile way.
examples: The dog *viciously* attacked a mail carrier.
He was *viciously* beaten and left on the street.
Critics attacked the movie *viciously*.

position: end
modifies: verbs

senses.gloss: As a winner; in a way that shows you have won.
examples: The team returned home *victoriously*.
She raised her fist *victoriously* as she crossed the finish line.
The army marched *victoriously* into the capital.

position: end — or mid before a participle (*vigilantly guarded*)
modifies: verbs of watching, guarding and checking

senses.gloss: Carefully watching for danger or problems.
examples: Security guards watched the crowd *vigilantly*.
Parents should monitor their kids' screen time *vigilantly*.
The border is *vigilantly* patrolled.

position: end — or mid before a verb (*vigorously denied*)
modifies: verbs of physical action, and of denying, defending and opposing

senses.gloss: With a lot of energy, force or determination.
examples: Stir the mixture *vigorously* for two minutes.
The company *vigorously* denied any wrongdoing.
She nodded *vigorously* when I asked if she wanted to come.

position: end — or mid before a verb
modifies: verbs

senses.gloss: In a way meant to hurt someone who you think has wronged you.
examples: The boss treated him *vindictively* after he complained.
She *vindictively* posted his private messages online.
They acted *vindictively*, not out of any sense of justice.

position: end — or mid before a participle (*violently attacked*); before its word for degree (*violently ill*)
modifies: verbs, past participles and a few adjectives (*ill*, *opposed*)

senses.gloss: With physical force that hurts or damages.
examples: The protest ended *violently*.
He was *violently* attacked in the parking lot.
The prisoners reacted *violently* to the new rules.

senses.gloss: Very strongly, suddenly or severely.
examples: She was *violently* ill after eating the shrimp.
The whole plane shook *violently*.
They disagree *violently* about politics.

position: before its word — before adjectives (*virulently racist*); mid or end with verbs
modifies: adjectives of hostility and verbs of attacking and opposing

senses.gloss: With strong hatred or bitter hostility.
examples: The pamphlet was *virulently* anti-immigrant.
Both parties *virulently* attacked the report.
She has *virulently* opposed the plan from the start.

position: mid or end — before adjectives and verbs (*viscerally frightening*, *react viscerally*)
modifies: verbs of reacting and feeling; adjectives of emotion

senses.gloss: In a deep, instinctive way that you feel in your body rather than think through.
senses.ru: нутром, на уровне инстинкта, всем существом
examples: I reacted *viscerally* to the photos from the war.
Fans respond *viscerally* to his music.
The movie is *viscerally* frightening.

position: mid — before participles and adjectives (*visibly shaken*)
modifies: past participles and adjectives of feeling; verbs of change
contrast: False friend: *visibly* means 'in a way you can see' (заметно, явно). Russian *видимо* in the sense 'apparently' is *apparently* or *evidently*: *Видимо, он устал* is *Apparently he was tired*, not *Visibly he was tired*.

senses.gloss: In a way that other people can clearly see.
examples: She was *visibly* upset when she left the meeting.
He was *visibly* shaken by the news.
Her father had *visibly* aged since the last time I saw him.

position: before its word — almost always *vitally important*
modifies: adjectives and participles: *important*, *necessary*, *needed*, *interested*

senses.gloss: Extremely; in a way that is essential.
examples: It's *vitally* important that you take this medicine every day.
Clean water is *vitally* needed in the region.
Teachers are *vitally* interested in the outcome of the vote.

position: mid or end — before *remember* and *recall*; after other verbs
modifies: verbs of remembering and describing; participles like *colored*

senses.gloss: Very clearly and in a lot of detail; with bright colors.
examples: I *vividly* remember the day we met.
The book describes life on the frontier *vividly*.
The birds were *vividly* colored.

position: any position — mid before a participle (*vocally opposed*); front with a comma for the singing sense
modifies: verbs of supporting and opposing; whole clauses

senses.gloss: Openly and loudly, in expressing an opinion.
examples: Parents have been *vocally* opposed to the new schedule.
She has spoken out *vocally* against the war.

senses.gloss: In terms of the voice or singing.
examples: *Vocally*, the song is very demanding.
The new album is *vocally* stronger than her last one.

position: mid or end
modifies: verbs of complaining, arguing, opposing and supporting

senses.gloss: Loudly and forcefully, in expressing an opinion.
examples: Fans complained *vociferously* about the referee's call.
The senator *vociferously* opposed the bill.
They argued *vociferously* for hours.

position: end — or mid before the verb
modifies: verbs

senses.gloss: Because you choose to, not because you are forced or paid.
examples: He left the company *voluntarily*.
The driver *voluntarily* surrendered to police.
Nobody is paid here — everyone works *voluntarily*.

position: end
modifies: verbs of eating and reading

senses.gloss: With a huge appetite, for food or for things like books and news.
examples: She reads *voraciously* — two or three books a week.
The kids ate *voraciously* after the game.
He follows the news *voraciously*.

position: end — after *stand*, *wade*, *sink*, usually before *in* or *into*
modifies: verbs of standing and moving in water, snow or mud
form: waist + deep; the same form is an adjective (*waist-deep water*)

senses.gloss: Deep enough to reach your waist.
examples: We waded *waist-deep* into the river.
The fishermen stood *waist-deep* in the cold water.
The soldiers marched *waist-deep* through the swamp.

position: end
modifies: verbs, mostly *smile*

senses.gloss: In a pale, weak or tired way, most often about a smile.
examples: She smiled *wanly* from her hospital bed.
He waved *wanly* as the bus pulled away.
The winter sun shone *wanly* through the clouds.

position: mid or end — usually before the verb
modifies: verbs of destroying, killing and disregarding

senses.gloss: Deliberately, without any reason, and with no care for the harm done.
examples: The vandals *wantonly* destroyed the benches in the park.
Soldiers were accused of *wantonly* killing civilians.
He *wantonly* ignored the safety of his passengers.

position: end — or mid before the verb
modifies: verbs of watching, approaching and reacting
contrast: Do not mix up *warily* (настороженно, from *wary*) and *wearily* (устало, from *weary*): *The cat watched the dog warily*, but *He climbed the stairs wearily*.

senses.gloss: Carefully, because you do not trust someone or expect danger.
examples: The cat watched the dog *warily*.
She eyed the stranger *warily*.
Investors are *warily* watching interest rates.

position: end — or mid before a participle (*warmly received*)
modifies: verbs of greeting, thanking and smiling; *dress*, *wrap*
contrast: In casual American speech *dress warm* is common, but *dress warmly* is the standard form in writing.

senses.gloss: In a friendly, kind way.
examples: Our hosts welcomed us *warmly*.
She smiled *warmly* at the children.
The movie was *warmly* received at the festival.

senses.gloss: So as to keep warm.
examples: Dress *warmly* — it's below zero out there.
The baby was *warmly* wrapped in a blanket.

position: end
modifies: verbs of spending and using

senses.gloss: In a way that uses more money, time or resources than needed.
examples: The agency spent the money *wastefully*.
We use water very *wastefully* in this town.
Tons of food are *wastefully* thrown away every day.

position: end
modifies: verbs
contrast: *Weakly* sounds exactly like *weekly* (еженедельно, раз в неделю).

senses.gloss: Without strength, force or energy.
examples: She smiled *weakly* and closed her eyes.
The patient's heart was beating *weakly*.
"I'm fine," he said *weakly*.

position: end — also front (*Wearily, she sat down*)
modifies: verbs
contrast: Do not mix up *wearily* (устало, from *weary*) and *warily* (настороженно, from *wary*).

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you are very tired or tired of something.
examples: He climbed the stairs *wearily*.
She sighed *wearily* and sat down.
"Not again," he said *wearily*.

position: any position — end for manner; before an adjective (*weirdly quiet*); front as a comment (*Weirdly, …*)
modifies: verbs, adjectives and whole clauses

senses.gloss: In a strange or unusual way.
examples: He's been acting *weirdly* all week.
The streets were *weirdly* quiet for a Saturday night.

senses.gloss: Surprisingly — commenting on a whole statement, often *weirdly enough*.
examples: *Weirdly*, I wasn't hungry at all.
*Weirdly* enough, nobody noticed the mistake.

position: end
modifies: verbs of motion, and *be*, *live*, *lie*
form: flat — the same form as the noun and adjective *west*
contrast: As an adverb it takes no preposition: *drive west*, *head west*, not *drive to west*. With *the* it is a noun: *in the west*, *to the west of town*. *Out west* is common in American speech for the western states: *They moved out west*.

senses.gloss: Toward or in the west.
senses.ru: на запад, к западу, на западе
examples: We drove *west* across Kansas.
The windows face *west*, so the sunsets are amazing.
The lake is about thirty miles *west* of the city.

position: end — or mid before a participle (*whimsically decorated*)
modifies: verbs and past participles

senses.gloss: In a playful, unusual and charming way.
examples: The café is *whimsically* decorated with old toys.
She named her cats *whimsically*, after famous poets.
The children's book is *whimsically* illustrated.

type: degree — in *a whole new*, *a whole different*, *a whole other*
position: before its word — between *a* and the adjective
modifies: the adjectives *new*, *different* and *other*
form: flat — the same form as the adjective *whole*
contrast: In *the whole day* (целый день) and *swallow it whole* (целиком), *whole* is an adjective. The adverb only strengthens *new*, *different* or *other* after *a*: *a whole new world* means 'a completely new world', not 'a whole world that is new'.

senses.gloss: Completely; used to stress how new or different something is.
examples: Having a baby is a *whole* new experience.
That's a *whole* different story.
Moving to Texas was a *whole* other adventure.

position: mid or end — *I wholeheartedly agree*, *I agree wholeheartedly*
modifies: verbs of agreeing, supporting and committing

senses.gloss: Completely and sincerely, with no doubts.
examples: I *wholeheartedly* agree with you.
We support the idea *wholeheartedly*.
She threw herself *wholeheartedly* into the new job.

position: end
modifies: verbs of buying and selling; verbs of rejecting, replacing and destroying
form: flat — the same form as the noun and adjective *wholesale*

senses.gloss: In large amounts at a lower price, usually to be sold again.
examples: We buy our coffee beans *wholesale*.
The bakery sells *wholesale* to restaurants and hotels.

senses.gloss: On a large scale, all at once, without picking out exceptions.
examples: The committee rejected the proposal *wholesale*.
The new owner replaced the staff almost *wholesale*.

position: before its word — before adjectives and participles; mid before a verb
modifies: adjectives, past participles and verbs
contrast: *Wholly* is often pronounced just like *holy* (святой). It is formal; in speech *completely* or *totally* is more usual. *Not wholly* means 'not entirely' (не совсем).

senses.gloss: Completely; entirely.
examples: I'm not *wholly* convinced by his story.
The company is *wholly* owned by the family.
That's a *wholly* different question.

position: before its word — before an adjective (*wickedly funny*); end for manner
modifies: adjectives, mostly of good qualities (*funny*, *smart*, *clever*); verbs like *grin* and *laugh*

senses.gloss: Very; extremely — about something clever or entertaining.
examples: The show is *wickedly* funny.
It's a *wickedly* clever plan.
Her comments were short and *wickedly* smart.

senses.gloss: In a mischievous or evil way.
examples: He grinned *wickedly* and grabbed the last cookie.
The villain laughed *wickedly*.

position: end — after *run*
modifies: the verb *run* (*run wild*)
form: flat — the same form as the adjective *wild*
contrast: Adverb *wild* lives mainly in the set phrase *run wild*. In *go wild* and *drive someone wild* it is an adjective. Everywhere else use *wildly*: *She waved wildly*, not *waved wild*.

senses.gloss: Without control or supervision, in *run wild*.
senses.ru: без удержу, без присмотра, как попало
examples: The kids ran *wild* while their parents talked.
Weeds are running *wild* in the backyard.
Don't let your imagination run *wild*.

position: end — for manner; before its word for degree (*wildly popular*)
modifies: verbs; adjectives like *popular*, *successful*, *inaccurate*, *different*

senses.gloss: In an uncontrolled, excited or violent way.
examples: The crowd cheered *wildly*.
She waved her arms *wildly* to get our attention.
The dog was barking *wildly* at the door.

senses.gloss: Extremely; very far from what is normal or correct.
examples: The show was *wildly* popular in the '90s.
His guess was *wildly* inaccurate.
Prices vary *wildly* from store to store.

position: mid — before a verb or participle (*willfully ignored*)
modifies: verbs of ignoring, violating and misleading

senses.gloss: On purpose, knowing that it is wrong or harmful.
examples: He *willfully* ignored the doctor's advice.
The company *willfully* violated safety laws.
She was accused of *willfully* misleading investors.

position: mid or end
modifies: verbs

senses.gloss: Because you want to or are happy to, without being forced.
examples: She *willingly* gave up her weekend to help.
Nobody would *willingly* live next to a landfill.
He went with the officers *willingly*.

position: end
modifies: verbs
form: rhyming compound, from old *will I, nill I* — 'whether I want or not'
contrast: Russian *волей-неволей* matches only the older second sense. Most Americans use *willy-nilly* informally to mean 'haphazardly' (как попало), so *They spent money willy-nilly* is about carelessness, not about being forced.

senses.gloss: Carelessly and without a plan; haphazardly.
examples: Don't just throw your clothes in the drawer *willy-nilly*.
The city approved new buildings *willy-nilly*.
Money was being spent *willy-nilly*.

senses.gloss: Whether you want to or not.
examples: We were dragged into the argument *willy-nilly*.
*Willy-nilly*, the town had to accept the new factory.

position: any position — end for manner; mid or front as a comment (*She wisely said nothing*)
modifies: verbs and whole clauses

senses.gloss: With good judgment; sensibly.
examples: Choose your friends *wisely*.
She *wisely* decided not to answer.
Spend your money *wisely* — it has to last all month.

position: end
modifies: verbs of looking, smiling and speaking

senses.gloss: With a slightly sad longing for something you do not have or have lost.
examples: She looked *wistfully* at the old photos.
"I used to live there," he said *wistfully*.
The kids stared *wistfully* out the window at the snow.

position: end — or before its word (*witheringly critical*)
modifies: verbs of looking and speaking; adjectives of criticism

senses.gloss: With scorn meant to make someone feel foolish or ashamed.
examples: She looked at him *witheringly* and walked away.
"Nice try," the teacher said *witheringly*.
The review was *witheringly* critical of the director.

position: end
modifies: verbs, mostly in set phrases: *inquire within*, *from within*, *the enemy within*
contrast: *Within* is far more common as a preposition with a noun after it: *within an hour* (в течение часа), *within the city limits* (в пределах города). The adverb, with nothing after it, is formal and lives mainly in set phrases like *inquire within* on a shop sign.

senses.gloss: Inside a building, a group or a person.
examples: Help wanted — inquire *within*.
Real change has to come from *within*.
The biggest threat was the enemy *within*.

position: end — or mid before a participle (*wittily written*)
modifies: verbs of speaking and writing; past participles

senses.gloss: In a clever and funny way.
examples: The speech was *wittily* written.
He answered the reporter's question *wittily*.
She *wittily* summed up the whole debate in one line.

position: mid — before the verb; often in *wittingly or unwittingly*
modifies: verbs
contrast: Much rarer than its opposite *unwittingly* (невольно, по незнанию), and usually paired with it: *wittingly or unwittingly*.

senses.gloss: Knowing what you are doing; on purpose.
examples: *Wittingly* or not, she helped the scammers.
He would never *wittingly* hurt anyone.
Many people *wittingly* or unwittingly share false stories online.

position: before its word
modifies: negative adjectives and participles: *inadequate*, *unprepared*, *understaffed*

senses.gloss: Very badly; to a sad or shameful degree.
examples: The hospital is *woefully* understaffed.
We were *woefully* unprepared for the storm.
The school's budget is *woefully* inadequate.

position: end — for manner; before its word as an intensifier (*wonderfully warm*)
modifies: verbs and adjectives

senses.gloss: Very well; in a way that is very pleasing.
examples: The kids behaved *wonderfully* at dinner.
It's a *wonderfully* funny book.
Everything worked out *wonderfully* in the end.

position: end
modifies: verbs of acting, speaking and moving

senses.gloss: Stiffly, without natural feeling or expression.
examples: The actors delivered their lines *woodenly*.
He smiled *woodenly* for the cameras.
She read the statement *woodenly*, without looking up.

position: any position — mid before the verb, end, or front with a comma
modifies: verbs

senses.gloss: Without saying anything.
examples: She *wordlessly* handed him the letter.
He nodded *wordlessly* and left the room.
*Wordlessly*, they walked back to the car.

position: end
modifies: verbs of asking, looking and speaking

senses.gloss: In a way that shows you are worried.
examples: "Is she okay?" he asked *worriedly*.
Her mother kept glancing *worriedly* at the clock.
The pilot looked *worriedly* at the fuel gauge.

position: mid — before a participle (*wrongfully convicted*)
modifies: past participles and verbs of accusing, arresting, firing and convicting
contrast: *Wrongfully* is about injustice or breaking the law: *wrongfully convicted*, *wrongfully fired*. For a simple mistake use *wrongly* or *incorrectly*: *The name was spelled wrongly*.

senses.gloss: Unfairly or illegally.
examples: He spent twenty years in prison after being *wrongfully* convicted.
She sued the company, claiming she was *wrongfully* fired.
The family says their son was *wrongfully* arrested.

position: end — or mid before the verb
modifies: verbs of smiling, speaking and writing

senses.gloss: With dry, slightly mocking humor.
examples: "Well, that went well," she said *wryly*.
He smiled *wryly* when he saw the mistake.
The book *wryly* describes life in a small office.

position: mid or end
modifies: verbs of guarding, defending, enforcing and pursuing

senses.gloss: With great energy and devotion to a cause or duty.
examples: She *zealously* guards her privacy.
The new manager enforced the rules *zealously*.
Lawyers must represent their clients *zealously*.
